newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek o/n, tomnext maintain firm tone in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek o/n, tomnext maintain firm tone in late trade.

text.p: The injection of overnight funds by the Bank of Greece at 13.40 percent was insufficient to allievate a liquidity shortage and deals between 14 and 15.40 percent took place, dealers said.
Longer tenors were holding morning levels.

"It was a difficult day with trading activity concentrating on overnight deals," said a money trader at a state bank. "The market is short and although the central bank's intervention helped a lot it did not cure the shortage."
The Bank of Greece offered overnight funds at 13.40 percent and additional liquidity on collateral of state securities issued on September 30.
Some banks had exhausted their overnight lines with the central bank and were compelled to resort to borrowing from other banks at high rates, dealers said.
"The market will be short tomorrow as well," said a trader at a foreign bank. "Forex inflows will help liquidity."
About 85 million ecus were sold today at the central bank's fixing, dealers said.
Greece issued three-, six- and 12-month T-bills at unchanged yields of 11.90, 12.10 and 12.70 percent respectively on Monday.
The mark was quoted at 157.82/87 drachmas from Monday's 157.900 fix, the dollar at 240.98/08 drachmas from 241.300 and the Ecu at 301.02/12 from 301.250 drachmas.
